mappings.note: What message the soldier gives his countrymen (to be ready to die for the country). The stem names the soldier-to-nation direction, which is C-H2.1-LO-9, rather than the reader's own response under C-H2.1-LO-11.
What the country takes pride in. Mapped LO-4 on the stem's content; its key is wrong -- the flagged option is 'किसी पर नहीं' where the poem's answer is the soldiers -- and that is reported.

When a soldier's challenges increase. Mapped LO-4 as a comprehension item about the soldier's life; its flagged answer ('when he marries') does not follow from the गीत and is reported as a key defect.
What the soldiers gave to defend the country (their lives). Factual recall, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
What counts as a जश्न for the soldiers (शहादत). A 1-mark recall of the song's claim; the item asking the तात्पर्य of 'फ़तह का जश्न' is LO-5, and the line explications are C-H2.1-LO-10.
What the earth is compared to (a bride). Identifying the comparison, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
The भाव of 'जान देने की रुत' -- the rare chance to give one's life for the country. Line read for its sacrifice, so C-H2.1-LO-10, matching the identical item earlier in the chapter.
Which time comes again and again in life (the time of living) -- the converse of the song's 'जान देने की रुत रोज आती नहीं'. Content recall, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
Names of Kaifi Azmi's collections (झंकार, आख़िर-ए-शब, आवारा सजदे). Bibliographic fact about the poet, so C-H2.3.
Why the earth is compared to a bride. Construing the metaphor, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.1-LO-10.
Whom 'साथियो' addresses and which काफ़िला must be carried forward. The charge laid on the countrymen makes it C-H2.1-LO-9 rather than the bare address gloss under LO-5.
